MY WEATHER JOURNAL

Build a Toy Shelter

Design, test and improve a little roof that helps keep a washable toy dry.

Look, then try.

Use a small box and a roof material over a tray. With adult help, pour a little water over the roof and inspect inside. Change one feature and test again with a similar amount of water. This indoor model is not a shelter for people.

Start drawing and writing below

Open the worksheet to print or save

Observe with a grown-up from a safe indoor spot. Never look directly at the sun. Stay indoors during storms. For the toy shelter, test over a tray with adult help and keep devices dry.

Use a finger, stylus or mouse in each drawing box. Type below it, or ask a grown-up to write your words. Your work stays in this tab. Save before refreshing or leaving.

ACTIVITY 1

My first shelter

Draw the roof, box and toy. Label your materials.

ACTIVITY 2

Test and improve

Describe what got wet. Draw one change to your design.

Your ideas belong here. There is no score.

What are we learning?

Testing helps us improve a design. Comparing one change at a time makes it easier to explain what helped.
